questionText: What does CCCRN stand for?

options.A: Centre for Community Care and Research Network
options.B: Center for Clinical Care and Clinical Research
options.C: Centre for Clinical Records and National Research

questionText: What is the primary mission of CCCRN?

options.A: To promote best practices in healthcare delivery and research using locally adapted health systems strengthening approaches.
options.B: To provide commercial healthcare insurance.

questionText: What does BRIDGE-N stand for?

options.A: Building Resilient Integrated Delivery of HIV, TB, Malaria and MNCH Services for Government-led Effective Health System in Nigeria.
options.B: Building Rural Integrated Development and General Education in Nigeria.
options.C: Basic Research and Integrated Development for Government Healthcare.
options.D: Building Resilient Institutions for Disease Management.

questionText: Which four health areas are covered by BRIDGE-N?

options.A: HIV, TB, malaria and MNCH.
options.B: HIV, cancer, diabetes and surgery.
options.C: Malaria, hypertension, kidney disease and cancer.
options.D: TB, immunization, surgery and mental health only.

questionText: What is the primary purpose of a Client Navigator?

options.A: To diagnose diseases.
options.B: To help clients access health services, attend appointments, maintain continuity of care and complete referrals.

questionText: Which of the following best describes client-centred care?

options.A: Providing services without considering clients' needs.
options.B: Respecting clients' needs, preferences, dignity and rights when providing support.
options.C: Making all decisions without consulting clients.
options.D: Giving priority only to clients who can pay.

questionText: Why is integration of health services important?

options.A: It makes it easier for clients to access related health services and improves continuity of care.
options.B: It eliminates the need for medical professionals.
options.D: It removes the need for patient records.

questionText: What does client navigation mean?

options.A: Directing clients to appropriate health services and helping them complete the care process.
options.B: Providing transportation to every patient.

questionText: What is linkage to care?

options.A: Connecting a client who needs a health service to the appropriate provider or facility.
options.B: Discharging all patients.
options.D: Registering patients without providing further support.

questionText: What is continuity of care?

options.A: Ensuring clients receive consistent and appropriate health services over time.
options.B: Providing treatment only once.
options.C: Stopping treatment when a client misses an appointment.
options.D: Referring all clients to different hospitals.

questionText: What is the purpose of appointment tracking?

options.A: To monitor scheduled visits and identify clients who miss appointments.
options.B: To increase hospital waiting time.
options.C: To identify patients who should be discharged.

questionText: What is a missed appointment?

options.A: A client attending a clinic early.
options.B: A client failing to attend a scheduled health appointment.

questionText: What does treatment interruption mean?

options.A: A client temporarily or permanently stops prescribed treatment without an appropriate clinical decision.
options.B: A client attends all scheduled appointments.
options.D: A health worker updates a register.

questionText: What should a Client Navigator do when a client misses an appointment?

options.A: Publicly announce the client's name.
options.B: Follow approved follow-up procedures, use an authorised and confidential communication method, establish the reason for the missed appointment and support return to care.
options.C: Immediately remove the client from the programme.
options.D: Disclose the client's medical condition to neighbours.

questionText: What is a follow-up in client navigation?

options.A: Contacting or otherwise checking on a client after an appointment, referral or service to determine whether further support is needed.
options.B: Discharging a client without assessment.

questionText: What is a treatment adherence support activity?

options.A: Encouraging clients to follow their prescribed treatment plans and helping address barriers to adherence.
options.B: Changing a client's prescribed medication.
options.C: Forcing a client to take medication.

questionText: Which of the following is an important quality of an effective Client Navigator?

options.A: Poor communication.
options.B: Confidentiality, empathy, patience and good communication.

questionText: What is a referral in healthcare?

options.A: Sending or directing a client to another appropriate health professional, service or facility for care.
options.B: Discharging a patient without treatment.
options.D: Transferring a patient without informing anyone.

questionText: What is a closed-loop referral?

options.A: Referring a client and assuming that the process is complete.
options.B: Referring a client, confirming that the intended service was accessed, and documenting feedback or the outcome.
options.C: Referring a client without a referral record.
options.D: Sending a client to multiple facilities without follow-up.

questionText: Which of the following is the correct referral process?

options.A: Identify need → refer client → confirm service received → document outcome.
options.B: Refer client → forget about the client.

questionText: A client is referred to a TB clinic from an HIV clinic. What should the Client Navigator do?

options.A: Assume the client attended the TB clinic.
options.B: Follow up according to approved procedures to confirm that the client accessed TB services and document the outcome.

questionText: Why is referral documentation important?

options.A: It provides evidence of the referral, supports follow-up and helps ensure continuity of care.
options.B: It increases paperwork without any purpose.
options.D: It prevents clients from accessing other services.

questionText: What should happen if a client does not complete a referral?

options.A: Ignore the client.
options.B: Identify barriers, communicate with the appropriate team and support completion through approved procedures.

questionText: What does HIV stand for?

options.A: Human Immunodeficiency Virus.
options.B: Human Infection Virus.

questionText: What does ART stand for?

options.A: Antiretroviral Therapy.
options.B: Advanced Research Treatment.

questionText: What is the primary purpose of antiretroviral therapy?

options.A: To cure every HIV infection.
options.B: To suppress HIV replication and support long-term health.

questionText: What is the meaning of viral load?

options.A: The amount of HIV genetic material in a person's blood.
options.B: The number of medications taken daily.
options.C: The number of white blood cells only.
options.D: The amount of sugar in the blood.

questionText: What does viral suppression mean?

options.A: HIV has been completely eliminated from the body.
options.B: HIV has been reduced to a very low level through effective treatment.
options.C: The client has stopped taking medication.
options.D: The client no longer requires medical follow-up.

questionText: What is the appropriate role of a Client Navigator when supporting someone living with HIV?

options.A: Disclose the person's HIV status to family members without permission.
options.B: Support appointment attendance, treatment continuity, referrals and confidential follow-up.

questionText: What does ART adherence mean?

options.A: Taking prescribed antiretroviral medication according to the healthcare provider's instructions.
options.B: Taking medication only when symptoms appear.
options.C: Stopping medication when the client feels healthy.

questionText: What does TB stand for?

options.A: Tuberculosis.
options.B: Total Blood.

questionText: How is pulmonary tuberculosis mainly transmitted?

options.A: Through mosquito bites.
options.B: Through infectious airborne particles released by a person with infectious TB.

questionText: Which of the following may be symptoms of pulmonary TB?

options.A: Persistent cough, fever, night sweats and weight loss.
options.B: Only headache.

questionText: What should a Client Navigator do when a client reports symptoms suggestive of TB?

options.A: Prescribe TB medication.
options.B: Support prompt referral to an appropriate health facility for assessment and testing, following approved procedures.

questionText: Why is TB treatment adherence important?

options.A: It supports treatment success and reduces the risk of treatment failure and drug resistance.
options.B: It increases the duration of illness.
options.C: It eliminates the need for medical supervision.

questionText: Which mosquito transmits malaria?

options.A: Female Anopheles.
options.B: Housefly.

questionText: What is the importance of malaria testing before treatment?

options.A: To support appropriate diagnosis and treatment decisions.
options.B: To determine a person's blood group.

questionText: What does MNCH stand for?

options.A: Maternal, Newborn and Child Health.
options.B: Medical Nursing and Community Health.

questionText: What does ANC stand for?

options.A: Antenatal Care.
options.B: Annual Nursing Census.

questionText: What is the importance of antenatal care?

options.A: Monitoring maternal and fetal health during pregnancy and identifying possible complications.
options.B: Providing treatment only after childbirth.

questionText: What is postnatal care?

options.A: Care provided to the mother and newborn after childbirth.
options.B: Care provided only before pregnancy.

questionText: What should a Client Navigator do when a pregnant woman misses an important antenatal appointment?

options.A: Ignore her.
options.B: Follow up confidentially and support her return to antenatal services in accordance with approved procedures.

questionText: What is patient confidentiality?

options.A: Sharing patient information with friends.
options.B: Protecting a client's personal and medical information from unauthorised disclosure.
options.D: Giving patient records to community members.

questionText: Can a Client Navigator disclose a client's HIV status to a neighbour?

options.A: Yes.
options.B: Only when the neighbour requests it.
options.C: No, not without proper legal authority or the client's valid consent.
options.D: Yes, if the neighbour is curious.

questionText: What should you do before contacting a client about a sensitive health appointment?

options.A: Contact anyone who answers the phone.
options.B: Follow the approved communication and consent procedures, including checking whether the contact method is safe.
options.C: Send the client's diagnosis to a group chat.
options.D: Ask the client's neighbours to intervene.

questionText: What is informed consent?

options.A: Giving a client information about a proposed activity and obtaining their voluntary agreement.
options.B: Forcing a client to accept a service.
options.C: Making decisions without informing a client.

questionText: What is stigma in healthcare?

options.A: Discrimination or negative attitudes towards people because of a health condition or other characteristic.
options.B: Providing respectful care.

questionText: How should a Client Navigator treat a client living with HIV?

options.A: With discrimination.
options.B: With respect, dignity, empathy and confidentiality.

questionText: What should you do if a client refuses a referral?

options.A: Force the client to attend.
options.B: Respect the client's decision, explore concerns, provide appropriate information and document the interaction according to procedures.
options.D: Remove the client from all services.

questionText: What is the appropriate action when a client reports abuse or a safeguarding concern?

options.A: Ignore the report.
options.B: Follow safeguarding procedures, prioritise immediate safety and report through authorised channels.
options.C: Share the story with other clients.
options.D: Investigate and confront the alleged perpetrator independently.

questionText: Which of the following best describes the difference between the two roles?

options.A: They are exactly the same.
options.B: A Client Navigator provides broader integrated health-service navigation, while a Maternal and Child Peer Navigator has a specialized maternal and child peer-support function.
options.C: A Client Navigator only works in laboratories.
options.D: A Maternal and Child Peer Navigator only handles pharmacy supplies.

questionText: If a pregnant woman needs antenatal care, what should a Client Navigator do?

options.A: Refuse to assist because the position is not a maternal health position.
options.B: Support her linkage to the appropriate antenatal service within the approved scope and coordinate with the relevant specialized team where necessary.

questionText: A client living with HIV has missed two scheduled clinic appointments. What should you do first?

options.A: Delete the client's records.
options.B: Follow the approved, confidential follow-up process and establish the reason for the missed appointments.
options.C: Disclose the client's HIV status to relatives.

questionText: A client has been referred from one facility to another but has not attended the receiving facility. What should you do?

options.A: Close the referral as completed.
options.B: Follow up through approved procedures, identify barriers and support completion of the referral.
options.D: Change the referral record to successful.

questionText: A client tells you that transport costs are preventing them from attending appointments. What is the best response?

options.A: Blame the client.
options.B: Understand the barrier and explore available approved support or alternative service arrangements with the relevant team.
options.D: Promise money from project funds without authorisation.

questionText: A client does not want to disclose their HIV status to family members. What should you do?

options.A: Tell the family anyway.
options.B: Respect the client's confidentiality and provide support without unauthorised disclosure.

questionText: A client complains that a health worker treated them disrespectfully. What should you do?

options.A: Ignore the complaint.
options.B: Listen respectfully, document and escalate through the appropriate complaint or feedback mechanism.

questionText: A client needs both HIV and TB services. What is your responsibility?

options.A: Refer the client to only one service.
options.B: Support linkage to both appropriate services, coordinate with relevant facility teams and promote continuity of care.
options.C: Diagnose the client with both diseases.
options.D: Tell the client to visit any facility without guidance.

questionText: You are unable to reach a client by telephone. What should you do?

options.A: Share the client's phone number publicly.
options.B: Document the unsuccessful attempt and follow the approved alternative follow-up procedures.
options.C: Delete the client from the register.
options.D: Assume the client has completed treatment.

questionText: A client becomes angry during a follow-up interaction. What should you do?

options.A: Respond aggressively.
options.B: Remain calm, listen actively, demonstrate empathy and seek appropriate assistance if necessary.

questionText: A client is referred to a laboratory but has not received the required test result. What should you do?

options.A: Create a result yourself.
options.B: Coordinate with the appropriate laboratory or facility team to establish the status and support the next step.
options.D: Give the client an assumed result.

questionText: What should you do when a client's contact details change?

options.A: Update the approved records according to procedures and consent requirements.
options.B: Continue using the old number indefinitely.
options.D: Share the new number with everyone.
